_metadata.rubric: x02 rubric (owner style examples, clicks-when-explained bar, fewer phrase-joins, mechanism labelled, explanation checked), 2026-10-19
_metadata.independence: I read only the instructions file and x02-d-review-input.json; no other repository file, search, web or paid API was used.

hints.reason: BONE: the humerus is the upper-arm bone where the funny bone sits; FUNNY: it sounds like 'humorous', a classic pun that clicks instantly.

best_available.why: A well-loved pun that hits both words cleanly and the explanation is accurate.

hints.reason: ANGEL: angel food cake; DEVIL: devil's food cake; a phrase-join, but both are instantly familiar U.S. cakes and the light/dark opposites make it satisfying.
ANGEL and DEVIL: the iconic cartoon conscience scene with an angel on one shoulder and a devil on the other; one image covers both.

best_available.why: A scene rather than a phrase-join, exactly the style the owner wants more of, and it lands both sides at once.

pairs.pair_note: Two good options; SHOULDER is preferred under the fewer-phrase-joins guidance.

hints.reason: COCKROACH: Raid, the famous bug spray; VIKING: Viking raids; an odd pair joined neatly by a brand/verb double meaning.

best_available.why: Unexpected pairing resolved by a clean double meaning everyone knows.

hints.reason: INTERNET: browser cookies that track you; JAR: the cookie jar; a double meaning in the same spirit as the owner's INTERNET + AFRICA -> SAFARI.
hints.fix: Name the jar in the explanation, e.g. 'One kind of cookie lives in the jar; the other kind tracks your browsing.'

best_available.why: Natural, broad double meaning; only the explanation needs to mention the jar.

pairs.pair_note: Good; explanation currently never mentions JAR.

hints.reason: HELICOPTER: 'chopper' is simply the everyday slang synonym for helicopter, which the rubric fails; AXE: an axe chops, but calling an axe a 'chopper' is looser.

best_available.why: The double meaning is fun, but it is a plain synonym of HELICOPTER; served only if the synonym rule is relaxed for double meanings.

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: strict rule reading makes this a FAIL; a lenient reading would make it BORDERLINE. Needs a non-synonym hint.

hints.reason: REFEREE: black-and-white striped shirts; ZEBRA: its stripes; and refs really are nicknamed 'zebras' in U.S. sports.

best_available.why: Clean shared property with a true bonus fact in the explanation.

hints.reason: CUSHION: the stuffing inside it; TURKEY: Thanksgiving stuffing; a tidy double meaning with a funny eat-it/sit-on-it contrast.

best_available.why: Natural double meaning, both sides instant.

hints.reason: LADY: Lady Gaga; RADIO: Queen's 'Radio Ga Ga', which really inspired her stage name; the true origin fact lifts it above a plain name-join.

best_available.why: Pop culture with a satisfying true backstory.

pairs.pair_note: Radio Ga Ga is less known to younger players, but the explanation makes it click.

hints.reason: GUARDIAN: Groot is one of the Guardians of the Galaxy; TREE: he is a tree creature; one character covers both, in the BARNEY style.

best_available.why: Exactly the owner's character-links-both style.

hints.reason: DOOR: knock on the door; WOOD: knock on wood; fair and familiar but a 'knock on ___' fill-in of the HAT/MAGIC -> TRICK kind the owner wants fewer of.

best_available.why: Fair and instantly understood; only held back by the phrase-join guidance.

pairs.pair_note: Usable fallback; a non-phrase idea would be preferred.

hints.reason: CANAL: the Panama Canal; HAT: the Panama hat, which many younger U.S. players will not know; a name-only join, though the Ecuador aside is a nice touch and accurate.

best_available.why: Fair and factually careful; the hat side is the soft spot.

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: could pass if Panama hat is judged broadly familiar.

hints.reason: CHEESE: holey Swiss cheese; KNIFE: the Swiss Army knife; both genuinely come from Switzerland, so it is a shared origin rather than a bare name-join.

best_available.why: Both sides instant and the explanation is true.

hints.reason: HOCKEY and CUP: the Stanley Cup is hockey's trophy, with a bonus nod to the viral Stanley tumbler cup that makes the explanation playful.

best_available.why: Broad U.S. reference with a current pop-culture wink.

hints.reason: CHRISTMAS and THIEF: How the Grinch Stole Christmas; one character covers both directly.

best_available.why: The natural perfect hint.

hints.reason: JOKE and ROAD: 'Why did the chicken cross the road?', the most famous joke there is; the punchline explanation is a charming touch.

best_available.why: Iconic shared reference with a witty explanation.

hints.reason: MIND: an open mind; PARACHUTE: it has to open; the 'minds are like parachutes' saying ties them into a satisfying shared property.

best_available.why: Works even without the saying, and the saying makes it click.

pairs.pair_note: OPEN may tempt other board words (door, jar), but generic is not a reason to reject.

hints.reason: WALL and FALL: Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall and had a great fall; one nursery rhyme covers both.

best_available.why: Instantly recognised, and the pair even rhymes like the verse.

hints.reason: WHEEL: the Ferris wheel; FAIR: a fairground staple, and the explanation's true fact (built for the 1893 Chicago World's Fair) adds a nice click.

best_available.why: Natural and backed by an accurate history fact.

hints.reason: SCALE: Libra's scales; SCORPION: Scorpio; both are zodiac symbols and really are adjacent signs, though the explanation never says which symbol is which.
hints.fix: Spell out the symbols, e.g. 'Libra's scales and Scorpio's scorpion sit side by side in the zodiac.'

best_available.why: Fair, broad, and the neighbour fact is true.

pairs.pair_note: Watch boards with other zodiac creatures (fish, crab, lion, bull, ram).

hints.reason: FISHING: a fishing lure; SIREN: the mythical sirens lured sailors; noun/verb double meaning with a nice mythic twist on SIREN.

best_available.why: Elegant double meaning that recasts SIREN away from alarms.

hints.reason: BAKERY: bread rolls; DICE: rolling the dice; clean noun/verb double meaning.

best_available.why: Fair, natural double meaning.

hints.reason: EYE: the pupil of the eye; SCHOOL: a pupil is a student; classic double meaning with a charming explanation.

best_available.why: Textbook double meaning, satisfying and fair.

hints.reason: BOND and COCKTAIL: James Bond's martini, 'shaken, not stirred'; one famous catchphrase covers both.

best_available.why: Iconic pop-culture line, lands immediately.

hints.reason: COFFEE: grinding beans; RAIL: a skateboard rail grind, a bit less universal but clear once explained.

best_available.why: Fair double meaning; the skate side is moderately familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Rail side leans on skate culture; still broadly understood.

hints.reason: NURSE: nurses wear scrubs; BRUSH: a scrub brush scrubs; the brush side is a touch softer but clicks on reading.

best_available.why: Clear double meaning, plus a TV-show echo.

hints.reason: BUS: to bus tables; WAITER: to wait tables; a phrase-join, but turning BUS from a vehicle into a restaurant verb is a genuine 'oh, nice' twist.
hints.fix: Use the word 'bus' so the link is explicit, e.g. 'A busser buses the tables; a waiter waits them.'

best_available.why: Exceptional phrase-join thanks to the BUS-as-verb reveal.

pairs.pair_note: Explanation should name the busing explicitly.

hints.reason: GIFT: gift wrap; MUMMY: wrapped in bandages; a funny shared property with a witty explanation.

best_available.why: Playful shared property; the 'only one is a nice surprise' line lands.

hints.reason: SWITCH: 'bait and switch'; WORM: worms are classic fishing bait; only the switch side is a phrase-join, and both sides are instant.

best_available.why: Fair, broad, and the idiom repurposes SWITCH nicely.

pairs.pair_note: Borderline-to-pass judgement under the phrase-join guidance; I lean pass because the worm side is a real property.

hints.reason: MARIO: Nintendo's famous plumber; LEAK: plumbers fix leaks; direct and fair.

best_available.why: Natural, accurate and broad.

hints.reason: POKEMON: Pikachu is the flagship Pokemon; DETECTIVE: the Detective Pikachu film and game, where he wears a deerstalker.

best_available.why: One character covers both, accurately.

pairs.pair_note: Solid; the POKEMON side is very direct.

hints.reason: OPERA: The Phantom of the Opera; ORGAN: the musical's famous pipe-organ riff and the Phantom at his organ.

best_available.why: Famous work linking both; the organ riff is instantly evoked.

hints.reason: HAMMER: Thor's hammer Mjolnir; MARVEL: Thor is a Marvel hero; explanation only covers the hammer side.
hints.fix: Mention Marvel, e.g. 'Only the worthy can lift Marvel's Thor's hammer, Mjolnir.'

best_available.why: Direct and broad character link.

hints.reason: SPONGEBOB and SNAIL: Gary is SpongeBob's meowing pet snail; one character covers both.

best_available.why: Accurate, broad character link with a fun detail.

hints.reason: TIGER: Tiger Woods the golfer; WOOD: a wood is a golf club; the hidden 'Tiger Woods' in the pair makes GOLF a satisfying reveal.

best_available.why: Two routes into golf, with the Tiger Woods name as a bonus.

hints.reason: NEWSPAPER: Clark Kent works at the Daily Planet; PLANET: Superman comes from planet Krypton; a neat double use of 'planet'.

best_available.why: Character link with a lovely planet/Daily Planet twist.

hints.reason: BENCH and CHOCOLATE: Forrest Gump on the bus-stop bench with his box of chocolates; one iconic scene covers both.

best_available.why: Iconic film scene; exactly the owner's preferred style.

hints.reason: TORNADO: Tornado Alley and Dorothy's twister in The Wizard of Oz; WHEAT: Kansas is the Wheat State; true facts plus a pop-culture nod.

best_available.why: Accurate place link with a Wizard of Oz bonus.
